\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Round Trip}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Switching.RoundTrip
\section{Overview}

This module proves the main round-trip property for the Razborov encoding used in the
switching lemma: decoding the encoding of a (bad) restriction recovers the original
restriction. From this round trip it follows that the encoding map is injective on bad
restrictions. The intermediate lemmas track invariants on the encoder/decoder state
(restrictions $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$) through the clause-processing fold.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Processing preserves free variables in the base restriction]
\lean{SwitchingLemma2.pcl_none_implies_rho_free}
\label{SwitchingLemma2.pcl_none_implies_rho_free}
\leanok
\uses{Literal, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits, SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits_rho_ne_none}
\difficulty{2}
Fix a number $n$ of variables. Let $\mathrm{lits}$ be a list of literals, each paired
with its position index in a clause; let $\mathrm{path}$ be a decision-tree path; let
$\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ be restrictions on the $n$ variables; and let $v$ be a variable.
Let $\rho_0'$ denote the updated restriction produced in place of $\rho_0$ by the
clause-processing procedure applied to $\mathrm{lits}$, $\mathrm{path}$, $\rho_0$, and
$\sigma$. If $\rho_0'$ leaves $v$ free, then $\rho_0$ already leaves $v$ free.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables, viewed as an ordered list of terms, in which
no term contains two distinct literals on the same variable. Fix restrictions $\rho_0$
and $\sigma$ such that $\sigma$ leaves free every variable that $\rho_0$ leaves free,
and suppose that $t_{\mathrm{clause}}$ is the first term of $f$, in list order, that is
not killed by $\rho_0$. Let $\rho_{\mathrm{enc}}$ be the restriction obtained as the
first component of the output of the Razborov encoding procedure applied to $f$ — with
width parameter $w$ and the given fuel and path arguments — started from $\rho_0$ and
$\sigma$, and let $\rho_{\mathrm{dec}}$ be any restriction that agrees with $\rho_0$ on
every variable that $\rho_0$ fixes and with $\rho_{\mathrm{enc}}$ on every variable that
$\rho_0$ leaves free. Then $t_{\mathrm{clause}}$ is also the first term of $f$, in list
order, that is not killed by $\rho_{\mathrm{dec}}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Filtering enumerated literals by free variables]
\lean{SwitchingLemma2.mem_filter_freeVars_zipIdx}
\label{SwitchingLemma2.mem_filter_freeVars_zipIdx}
\leanok
\uses{Literal, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction.freeVars}
\difficulty{2}
Fix a natural number $n$, a restriction $\rho_0$ on $n$ variables, and a list $t$ of
literals. Enumerate $t$ as the list of pairs $(\ell, i)$, where $\ell$ ranges over the
literals of $t$ and $i$ is the position of $\ell$ in $t$, and keep only those pairs
whose literal's variable is a free variable of $\rho_0$. Then every pair $(\ell, i)$
surviving this filter is itself one of the enumerated pairs of $t$, and its literal's
variable $v$ is free under $\rho_0$, meaning $\rho_0$ leaves $v$ unset.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[No auxiliary entry targets a still-free variable]
\lean{SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits_aux_ne_of_pcl_none}
\label{SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits_aux_ne_of_pcl_none}
\leanok
\uses{Literal, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits, SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits_rho_ne_none, SwitchingLemma2.zipIdx_drop_spec, Term}
\difficulty{5}
Let $t$ be a term on $n$ variables (a list of literals), let $L$ be a list of literals
each paired with a natural-number position, let $\pi$ be a path (a list of
variable–direction pairs), and let $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ be restrictions on $n$
variables. Suppose every pair in $L$ occurs in the indexed enumeration of $t$, so that
each $(l,i)\in L$ records a literal $l$ sitting at position $i$ of $t$. Run the
clause-processing procedure that consumes the free literals of $L$ against $\pi$
starting from $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$, and let $\rho_0'$ denote its updated
$\rho_0$-restriction and $A$ its list of clause auxiliary entries. If $\rho_0'$ leaves
the variable $v$ free, then for every entry $(i,d)\in A$ and every literal $l$ such that
deleting the first $i$ literals of $t$ leaves a nonempty list with head $l$, the
variable of $l$ is not $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Encoder first component matches the recursive step]
\lean{SwitchingLemma2.encode_go_fst_eq_rec}
\label{SwitchingLemma2.encode_go_fst_eq_rec}
\leanok
\uses{DNF, Literal, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction.freeVars, SwitchingLemma2.Term.killedBy, SwitchingLemma2.encode_go_fst_acc, SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits, Term}
\difficulty{4}
Fix a DNF formula $f$ on $n$ variables, two restrictions $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$, a fuel
budget, and a path $\mathrm{step} :: \mathrm{rest}$ consisting of a first
variable–direction pair $\mathrm{step}$ followed by a list $\mathrm{rest}$ of further
such pairs. Suppose $t_{\mathrm{clause}}$ is the first term of $f$ that is not killed by
$\rho_0$, and that, listing the literals of $t_{\mathrm{clause}}$ each tagged with its
position in the term and keeping only those whose variable is free under $\rho_0$, this
filtered list is nonempty, of the form $\mathit{fl} :: \mathit{fls}$. Then the first
component of the encoder run at fuel one greater on the whole path $\mathrm{step} ::
\mathrm{rest}$ coincides with the first component of the encoder run at the smaller fuel
started from the state obtained by processing the clause's free literals $\mathit{fl} ::
\mathit{fls}$ against that same path from $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Round-trip recovery of the restriction from a processed clause]
\lean{SwitchingLemma2.roundtrip_inv_hC'}
\label{SwitchingLemma2.roundtrip_inv_hC'}
\leanok
\uses{Literal, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.foldl_sigma_stable, SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits, SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits_aux_ne_nonfree, Term}
\difficulty{4}
Let $t$ be a term on $n$ variables, let $\mathit{lits}$ be a list of literals each
tagged with a position index, and let $\mathit{path}$ be a list of variable–direction
pairs. Let $\rho_0$, $\sigma$, and $\sigma_{\mathrm{dec}}$ be restrictions on $n$
variables, and suppose that every variable occurring in a literal of $\mathit{lits}$ is
free under $\rho_0$; that every tagged literal in $\mathit{lits}$ occurs at its recorded
position in $t$; that $\sigma$ is free at every variable that is free under $\rho_0$;
and that $\sigma_{\mathrm{dec}}$ agrees with $\sigma$ at every variable that $\rho_0$
fixes. Write $(\mathit{path}', \rho_0', \sigma', a)$ for the result of processing
$\mathit{lits}$ along $\mathit{path}$ starting from $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$, where $a$ is
the accumulated list of (position, direction) pairs. Then for every variable $v$ that
$\rho_0'$ fixes, the restriction obtained by folding over $a$ — starting from
$\sigma_{\mathrm{dec}}$ and, for each recorded pair with position $i$, freeing the
variable of the literal at position $i$ in $t$ (and leaving the restriction unchanged
when $i$ lies beyond the end of $t$) — agrees with $\sigma$ at $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Reconstructing the processed restriction from its auxiliary data]
\lean{SwitchingLemma2.roundtrip_inv_hD'}
\label{SwitchingLemma2.roundtrip_inv_hD'}
\leanok
\uses{Literal, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.foldl_rho_stable, SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits, SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits_foldl_rho_eq_of_set, SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits_rho_stable, Term}
\difficulty{4}
Let $t$ be a term on $n$ variables (a list of literals), let $\mathit{lits}$ be a list
of literals each paired with a position index, let a decision-tree path be given, and
let $\rho_0$, $\sigma$, and $\rho_{0,\mathrm{dec}}$ be restrictions on the $n$
variables. Assume that every literal in $\mathit{lits}$ has its variable left free by
$\rho_0$, that every pair in $\mathit{lits}$ occurs in the indexed enumeration of $t$
(each literal of $t$ paired with its position), and that $\rho_{0,\mathrm{dec}}$ agrees
with $\rho_0$ at every variable that $\rho_0$ fixes. Write $\rho_0^{\ast}$ for the
restriction and $A$ for the auxiliary list of index–direction pairs produced by
processing $\mathit{lits}$ against the path starting from $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$.
Reconstruct a restriction from $\rho_{0,\mathrm{dec}}$ by folding over $A$: for each
pair $(i,b)$, if deleting the first $i$ literals of $t$ leaves a nonempty list, set the
variable of that list's head literal to $b$, and otherwise leave the restriction
unchanged. Then at every variable $v$ at which $\rho_0^{\ast}$ is defined, this
reconstructed restriction and $\rho_0^{\ast}$ take the same value.
\end{lemma}

\uses{DNF, DNF.width, Literal, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction.freeVars, SwitchingLemma2.Term.killedBy, SwitchingLemma2.encode_go_acc, SwitchingLemma2.encode_go_fst_sigma_indep_at_free, SwitchingLemma2.encode_go_snd_sigma_indep, SwitchingLemma2.find_clause_preserved_in_encode, SwitchingLemma2.foldl_rho_stable, SwitchingLemma2.foldl_sigma_stable, SwitchingLemma2.mem_filter_freeVars_zipIdx, SwitchingLemma2.pcl_none_implies_rho_free, SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits, SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits_aux_ne_of_pcl_none, SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits_sigma_none_of_rho_none, SwitchingLemma2.processEntries_of_processClauseLits, SwitchingLemma2.roundtrip_base, SwitchingLemma2.roundtrip_inv_hC', SwitchingLemma2.roundtrip_inv_hD', SwitchingLemma2.term_length_le_width}
\difficulty{7}
Fix a DNF formula $f$ on $n$ variables whose width is at most $w$ and in which no term
repeats a variable (within a single term, any two literals on the same variable are
equal). Given a fuel budget, a partial decision path, and restrictions $\rho_0$ and
$\sigma$, let the encoding procedure, started with empty auxiliary data, return a
restriction $\rho^\ast$ together with an output list $c$; let $D$ denote the decoding
procedure run on $c$ with a fuel budget $m$ and starting restrictions
$\sigma_{\mathrm{dec}}$ and $\rho_{0,\mathrm{dec}}$. Suppose that $\sigma$ is free
wherever $\rho_0$ is free; that on every variable left free by $\rho_0$ both
$\sigma_{\mathrm{dec}}$ and $\rho_{0,\mathrm{dec}}$ agree with $\rho^\ast$; that on
every variable fixed by $\rho_0$ one has $\sigma_{\mathrm{dec}} = \sigma$ and
$\rho_{0,\mathrm{dec}} = \rho_0$; and that $m$ is at least one more than the length of
$c$. Then the restriction returned by $D$ equals $\sigma$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{2}
Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables whose width is at most $w$, and suppose that
within every term of $f$ any two literals naming the same variable are in fact equal.
Given a natural number serving as a step budget for the encoder, a finite list of
variable–value pairs, and a restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables, encoding $\rho$
relative to $f$ produces a list from which the decoder — run with a step budget one
larger than that list's length — recovers $\rho$ exactly.
\end{lemma}

Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables whose width is at most $w$, and suppose that
no term of $f$ contains two distinct literals on the same variable (within each term,
any two literals sharing a variable coincide). Let $\rho$ be a restriction that is bad
for $f$ at depth $d$, meaning the restriction of the Boolean function computed by $f$
along $\rho$ has decision-tree depth strictly greater than $d$. Writing $(\gamma,
\mathrm{aux})$ for the pair produced by the Razborov encoding of $f$, $w$, $d$, $\rho$,
the Razborov decoding of $(\gamma, \mathrm{aux})$ with parameters $f$ and $w$ returns
the original restriction $\rho$.
\end{lemma}

  {SwitchingLemma2.razborovDecode_encode}

  {pdf-b5e074215b9e-p002-b004,

\uses{DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, SwitchingLemma2.IsBadRestriction, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.razborovDecode_encode, SwitchingLemma2.razborovEncode}
\difficulty{2}
Fix a DNF formula $f$ on $n$ variables and parameters $w, d \in \bbn$, and suppose that
$f$ has width at most $w$ and that no term of $f$ repeats a variable — within any single
term, two literals sharing the same variable are identical. Under these hypotheses the
Razborov encoding with parameters $w$ and $d$ is injective on the restrictions that are
bad for $f$ at depth $d$: if $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ are restrictions, each bad for the
Boolean function computed by $f$ at depth $d$ (that is, the corresponding restricted
function has decision-tree depth exceeding $d$), and their Razborov encodings agree,
then $\rho_1 = \rho_2$.
\end{theorem}
